title: MDA / IMS-MDA / MIDAS
reason: scope:MDA: MDA means multiple displacement amplification. Dean et al., PMID 11959976, establish random exonuclease-resistant primers, Phi29 strand displacement and secondary priming, resolving these three local operations at amplification-component scope. The cited human-genome implementation also demonstrates why amplification is a representation of genomic sequence rather than a promise of perfectly preserved abundance. The family drawing explicitly contains o_s1, but the inspected MDA paper does not establish S1 treatment in that implementation; its member-specific applicability remains unresolved rather than being assigned to every MDA protocol.; scope:IMS-MDA: IMS-MDA is targeted immunomagnetic enrichment followed by MDA, not an alias for unenriched MDA. The protocol abstract establishes that combination; the original full text specifically supports Phi29/phosphorothioate-random-hexamer amplification and direct GenomiPhi amplification on retained beads without elution. Thus the generic template boundary in this schematic can represent accessible DNA of enriched bacteria, with capture and initial bacterial lysis upstream of the drawn priming. No claim is made that this input has been eluted or purified. Capture depends on intact bacteria; it does not measure all cell-free target DNA in the starting sample. Random priming can also copy residual non-target DNA, so enrichment is not perfect specificity. There is no depicted assignment to an individual bacterial cell. The cited implementation is C. trachomatis; broad applicability to all bacterial specimens or antibodies is not assumed. Applicability of the drawing’s S1 local instance to that implementation is not established by the inspected full text or protocol abstract.

method_scopes.rationale: MIDAS means microwell displacement amplification system. Gole et al., PMID 24213699, support the shared random-hexamer/Phi29 amplification component within separate microwells containing individual cells or nuclei. DNA association with an individual source is carried by well provenance and separate amplicon recovery; these compartments are upstream context, not newly drawn graph branches or a joint pooled reaction. At the declared schematic/component scope the generic genomic input and three amplification operations apply. For the supported MIDAS implementation, o_s1 is excluded: its paper converts hyperbranched amplicons into unbranched double-stranded DNA with random priming, DNA polymerase I and Ampligase before transposase-based library construction. That provides a correspondence in linearization purpose, not enzyme interchangeability. Correction c_midas_linearization records this specific resolution while retaining the diagram’s S1 route. Downstream sequencing can reveal single-cell genomic sequence and genomic copy-number changes; amplification bias still matters, and the assigned image depicts no computational readout operation.

research_questions.question: MDA means multiple displacement amplification. Dean et al., PMID 11959976, establish random exonuclease-resistant primers, Phi29 strand displacement and secondary priming, resolving these three local operations at amplification-component scope. The cited human-genome implementation also demonstrates why amplification is a representation of genomic sequence rather than a promise of perfectly preserved abundance. The family drawing explicitly contains o_s1, but the inspected MDA paper does not establish S1 treatment in that implementation; its member-specific applicability remains unresolved rather than being assigned to every MDA protocol.

IMS-MDA is targeted immunomagnetic enrichment followed by MDA, not an alias for unenriched MDA. The protocol abstract establishes that combination; the original full text specifically supports Phi29/phosphorothioate-random-hexamer amplification and direct GenomiPhi amplification on retained beads without elution. Thus the generic template boundary in this schematic can represent accessible DNA of enriched bacteria, with capture and initial bacterial lysis upstream of the drawn priming. No claim is made that this input has been eluted or purified. Capture depends on intact bacteria; it does not measure all cell-free target DNA in the starting sample. Random priming can also copy residual non-target DNA, so enrichment is not perfect specificity. There is no depicted assignment to an individual bacterial cell. The cited implementation is C. trachomatis; broad applicability to all bacterial specimens or antibodies is not assumed. Applicability of the drawing’s S1 local instance to that implementation is not established by the inspected full text or protocol abstract.
